successors.name: Wari Empire
successors.text: the Ica Department: the Río Grande de Nazca drainage and the Ica valley

ledger.x: c. 100 BCE: the Nazca culture begins on the south coast of Peru. Infobox 'Established: 100 BCE'; 'flourished from c. 100 BC to 800 AD' (Proto Nazca 100 BC-1 AD). Preceded by the Chavín and Paracas cultures.

c. 800: the Nazca culture ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 800 CE' while the text says 'by 750 AD the civilization had fallen completely'; Cahuachi's ceremonial use ended around 450-500 (Cahuachi page: severe drought, mudslides and earthquakes). Power shifted to the highlands with the Wari, dated about 650.

wars.name: Wari rise over the Nazca coast
wars.outcome: No fighting recorded: the page only says power 'shifted from the coast to the highlands with the Wari culture' (about 650); the Huari page calls Nasca 'under heavy Wari influence'.
